newsitem.title: UK: NWE GAS OIL SPREADS FIRM AS SUMMER LULL DRAGS ON.
newsitem.headline: NWE GAS OIL SPREADS FIRM AS SUMMER LULL DRAGS ON.

text.p: European gas oil traded steady to firm on Monday but volume was muted by seasonally poor demand, traders said.
"It's a really dead market," one said.

Outright values shed around $1.50 a tonne. The front month August IPE contract, which expires at midday on Tuesday, settled at $168.00 a tonne, down $1.50, while September settled at $169.75, down $1.25.

A cargo of German heating oil changed for the second half of August changed hands at a $1 premium to September IPE. Low sulphur diesel cargoes for French delivery were bid at around $4.50 and offered at $4.75 to $5 over September.
With two large Russian heating oil cargoes available spreads were assessed at around $0.560/$1.00 over September.
The market remained quiet, with those traders not yet on holiday concentrating on planning strategy for the autumn.
On barges a 2,000 tonne parcel of Rotterdam refinery heating oil moved at $1 over August IPE fob ARA. But many players concentrated on preparation for the August IPE delivery.
Low sulphur diesel barges were assessed slightly firmer at $5/$5.75 over August IPE cif ARA.
